criteria.criterion: After rotation state is initialized, an idempotent real-repo pass with no absent-key GETs leaves all committed bridge-state files byte-identical and does not advance HEAD. Verified by an integration test in a temporary git repository.
A pass with at most 20 absent-key GETs advances the same selected Jira-key stamps in `get_rotation.json` and the legacy inline fields. Verified by an integration test.
The explicit local binding-store commit path stages and commits both changed rotation files without `git add -A`. Verified by a real-git integration test.

An interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence produces the same rotation order as the all-new sequence. Verified by an integration test that fails if new binaries do not dual-write or if lookup is first-wins rather than `max()`.
A legacy bindings store containing inline stamps only preserves its rotation order. Verified by a focused unit test.
A legacy inline-only store materializes equivalent sidecar state on its next persisted save. Verified by a focused unit test.
`rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves `git status --porcelain` empty. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
`rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store does not create `get_rotation.json`. Verified through the real CLI subprocess.
`git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE` names `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`. Verified by the existing git-adapter characterization suite.
The regenerable-files documentation in `_store/push.py` names `get_rotation.json`. Verified by a focused characterization test.
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` remains at or below 800 lines. Verified by the repository module-size gate.
